$comment: Upstream @lenne.tech/nest-server DEVDEPENDENCIES that must land in a vendored project's `dependencies`. Vendoring copies upstream `dependencies` verbatim and does not read `peerDependencies` at all, so a package the framework imports at runtime while keeping it in devDependencies would never reach the production runtime. Entries here are matched against upstream `devDependencies` only — see `isVendorRuntimeDep`, consulted in the `upstreamDevDeps` loop in `extensions/server.ts` — and promoted into `dependencies`, preferring the upstream peer RANGE over the exact devDep pin where one exists, so a generated project still receives patch-level security fixes. A package that appears ONLY in upstream `peerDependencies` cannot be promoted by this list: listing it here is a silent no-op. One live case: the better-auth trio (declared as peerDependencies AND mirrored into devDependencies upstream; the mirror is what makes the promotion fire, so this list is the fallback if the starter ever stops declaring them itself). `find-file-up` was listed here until 2026-10-03 and never needed: no nest-server release from 8.x to 11.x imports it from src/ (only the dev script extras/sync-version.ts did), and 11.41.8 dropped the package altogether. Since nest-server 12.10.0 also `ai`, `@nestjs/ai` and `@nestjs/resilience`: OPTIONAL peers upstream (the AI module's AI SDK transport and agent-function bridge, loaded lazily), mirrored into its devDependencies, and named by the vendored core in literal `import()` calls — so a vendored project must declare them or its `tsc` fails with TS2307. The import-closure backfill would add them at the EXACT upstream lockfile version; listing them here promotes them with the upstream peer RANGE instead (`ai >=7.0.0 <8` follows the project's own `ai` patch line; the two 0.0.x ranges are as narrow as the framework's tested range, which it enforces at runtime). `runtimeHelpersSince` names, for an entry added ahead of a nest-server release, the release whose devDependencies first carry it. `__tests__/vendor-runtime-deps.test.ts` checks every entry against the sibling `../nest-server` checkout, and judges such an entry only once that checkout's version reaches it: a checkout from before the release (a teammate's, or `origin/develop` before the publish) would otherwise fail `npm test` over a package the CLI lists correctly. Keep the version in step with the release that actually ships the package; if it slips to a later one, raise it here too.
